title: Contractible affine-line constant defect vanishing
statement: Fix the algebraically closed field $k$ and finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $X=\mathbf A^1_k$, let $r\geq1$ be an integer, and let $i:Z=V(x^r)\hookrightarrow X$. Use the Rees specialization and defect cone $C_{X,Z}$ of [lem-trf-dnc-defect-proper-smooth-comparison]. For every finite $A$-module $L$, let $L_X$ and $L_Z$ denote the associated constant etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The canonical zero-section map $z^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}L_X\to L_Z$ is an isomorphism; equivalently, $C_{X,Z}(L_X)=0$.

proof.text: Write $T=\mathbf A^1_k$ with coordinate $a$, and $H:X\times T\to X$, $H(x,a)=ax$. Then $H^*(x^r)=a^rx^r$, so $H$ maps the closed pair $(X\times T,Z\times T)$ to $(X,Z)$. Its restrictions are $H_1=1_X$ and $H_0=i q$, where $q:X\to Z$ sends the coordinate of $k[x]/(x^r)$ to zero. In particular $H_0$ factors scheme-theoretically through $Z$, not only through its support. On $Z_{\mathrm{red}}=s$, $H$ is the projection. The Rees geometry node gives lifts of these pair maps and of the projection $\pi:X\times T\to X$, compatible with composition. For the projection the Rees algebra is the original Rees algebra with the free variable $a$ adjoined: its coefficients are the powers $(x^{rm})k[x,a]$. Thus the lifted projection is the affine-line projection over $\widetilde X_Z$, and is smooth by the affine-space smoothness node.

source.place: Definition 3.1.1, Example 3.1.2 and Lemma 3.1.3, construction of the lifted homotopy

proof.text: Put $P=z^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}L_X$ and let $\alpha:P\to L_Z$ be the canonical map. The comparison node defines it as $\theta_{L_Z}^{-1}\mathrm{BC}^*_{\widetilde i}$, where the constant-family unit $\theta_{L_Z}:L_Z\to\operatorname{sp}_{Z_D}L_Z$ is invertible. Let $\gamma:L_{N_{Z/X}}\to\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}L_X$ be the nearby-cycle unit, obtained from the constant sheaf on the whole deformation, and put $\beta=z^*\gamma:L_Z\to P$. Compatibility of exchange with this unit says $\mathrm{BC}^*_{\widetilde i}\,\beta=\theta_{L_Z}$. Consequently $\alpha\beta=1_{L_Z}$. Finiteness of $L$ makes its geometric generic constant sheaf constructible; nearby-cycle finiteness makes its specialization bounded constructible, and exact pullback preserves that property. No assertion of finite Tor amplitude for $L$ is needed.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.3, zero-section map (1.8) and its constant-sheaf unit section

proof.text: Let $w:s=Z_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow Z$ and $E=w^*P$. This is bounded constructible by the preceding step and constructible pullback. Both $w$ and $w\times1_T$ are universal homeomorphisms: after every base change their affine equations are quotients by the nilpotent ideal generated by $x$, with $x^r=0$; every prime contains a nilpotent ideal, so the quotient spectra have identical closed subsets. Etale topological invariance identifies their sheaf categories by exact quasi-inverse functors, hence also their derived categories termwise. In particular $w^*$ reflects isomorphisms of derived complexes. We may therefore prove $\alpha$ invertible after applying $w^*$. This passage keeps the original, possibly nonreduced, closed centre in the Rees deformation.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.3, identification of maps agreeing on the reduced centre

proof.text: Apply inverse-image nearby exchange to the lifted $H$, and then the inverse smooth exchange to the lifted $\pi$. Restrict on the special fibre to the reduced zero section $s\times T$. The starting pullback is $p^*E$ because $H$ on this reduced section is the projection; the ending pullback is $p^*E$ by the projection's smooth exchange. Since $H^*L_X=L_{X\times T}=\pi^*L_X$, this gives an endomorphism $\varphi:p^*E\to p^*E$ on $T$, where $p:T\to s$. For the section $a=c$, composition compatibility of exchange identifies $i_c^*\varphi$ with $w^*\varphi_c$, the zero-section exchange endomorphism for $\widetilde H_c$. Indeed $H_c=H\circ(1_X,i_c)$ and $\pi\circ(1_X,i_c)=1_X$; in the composite exchange for the latter, exchange for the section cancels the inverse projection exchange. This uses identity and composition laws for the specified exchange maps, without requiring the section exchange itself to be invertible globally.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.3, displayed parameter-family endomorphism and its fibre calculation

proof.text: For $c=1$, $H_1=1_X$ and identity compatibility gives $w^*\varphi_1=1_E$. For $c=0$, factor the pair map through $(Z,Z)$ as $X\xrightarrow q Z\xrightarrow i X$. The first exchange in pullback order is $\mathrm{BC}^*_{\widetilde i}$, hence after $\theta^{-1}$ it is $\alpha$. The second is exchange for $\widetilde q$. Compatibility with nearby units gives $\mathrm{BC}^*_{\widetilde q}(q_0^*\theta_{L_Z})=\gamma$ because $q^*L_Z=L_X$. On the reduced zero section, $q_0$ and the identity have the same map to $Z$ after composing with $w$, namely the unique reduced origin. Thus this second exchange, with the constant-family unit inserted, is $w^*\beta$. Composition compatibility now gives $w^*\varphi_0=(w^*\beta)(w^*\alpha)$. In particular the factorization through $L_Z$ is the one using the canonical map (1.8), rather than an unspecified abstract factorization.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.3, endpoint identities and factorization through (1.8)

proof.text: Apply the affine-line morphism-rigidity node to $P=Q=E$ and to the endomorphism $\varphi$ of Step 4. Its hypotheses hold: $E$ is bounded constructible on $s$, the field is algebraically closed, and $A$ has characteristic prime to $\operatorname{char}k$ in the sense that its torsion primes are invertible in $k$. It yields $i_0^*\varphi=i_1^*\varphi$. Step 5 therefore gives $(w^*\beta)(w^*\alpha)=1_E$, while Step 2 gives $(w^*\alpha)(w^*\beta)=1_{L_s}$. These equations make $w^*\alpha$ invertible. The exact equivalence of Step 3 reflects invertibility, proving that $\alpha:P\to L_Z$ is an isomorphism. Its cone $C_{X,Z}(L_X)$ is consequently zero, as claimed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q26-45c3e300a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, the new node lem-trf-constant-complex-a1-morphism-rigidity, every cited node's statement, and Varshavsky §3.1 (Def 3.1.1, Ex 3.1.2, Lemmas 3.1.3–3.1.4) and Claim 3.2.3. The item is Lemma 3.1.3 / Ex 3.1.2 generalized from F=Λ to any finite constant L, which is how the parent generic-zero-section node uses it; nothing is weakened. Coefficients are etale D^b_c with A=A_{E,n} and ℓ≠p, matching the comparison and specialization nodes. Step 1: H^*(x^r)=a^r x^r, H_0=i∘q with x↦0, q is a pair map to (Z,Z), and the projection lift is the A^1-projection, which is smooth. Steps 2 and 5: unit compatibility gives αβ=1 and w^*φ_0=(w^*β)(w^*α), using q̃_0zw=w; I checked both composites. Step 3: Z_red→Z is a universal homeomorphism, so w^* is an exact equivalence that reflects isomorphisms. Step 4: H̃_0 and π̃_0 agree on s×T, and σ_c with π σ_c=1 gives i_c^*φ=w^*φ_c by the composition and identity laws. Step 6: the two inverse equations give the isomorphism; the source shows only one of them. New node: true, because p^* is fully faithful on bounded complexes (H^q(A^1,M)=0 for q>0 and ℓ-torsion M). Checked on Hom(A,A)=A and Hom(A,A[1])=0. The ℓ≠p hypothesis is needed and is present. It is not a restatement and not a duplicate: prop-pur-a1-invariance needs ctf and rank-one shape, and lem-fd-affine-line-constant-cohomology has Q̄_ℓ coefficients. It is statement-only, with blueprint.from set and created.item correct. Accepted tool_uses: sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth, prop-constructible-pullback, thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance.
